# transformerpalettes

Colour palettes for R and ggplot2 based on Generation 1 Transformers:
Optimus Prime, Megatron, and every member and combined form of the core
combiner teams, from the Aerialbots and Superion to the Seacons and
Piranacon. Each character has a palette for the original toy and one for
the cartoon animation model, and some have one for the Marvel comic,
because the three often disagree about what colour a robot is. It works
the same way as packages like `wesanderson`: pick a character by name,
get a vector of hex colours, or drop a scale straight into a ggplot.
Because the combiner teams are sets of five or six figures, each team
also gives a ready-made categorical palette with one colour per member.

transformerpalettes is a fan project and is not affiliated with or
endorsed by Hasbro or Takara Tomy. Hex values are approximations of the
toys’ plastic, chrome and paint colours; see “How the palettes were
made” below.

## Browse online

Every palette, with its colours, toy photo and Transformers Wiki link,
is browsable and filterable at
<https://bmaitner.github.io/transformerpalettes/articles/browse.html>.
Each card has a **Suggest a change** link that opens a prefilled GitHub
issue, and there is a form to [request a
character](https://github.com/bmaitner/transformerpalettes/issues/new?template=new-character.yml)
who is not covered yet.
[`WISHLIST.md`](https://bmaitner.github.io/transformerpalettes/WISHLIST.md)
lists what is queued.

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("bmaitner/transformerpalettes")
```

## Usage

``` r

library(transformerpalettes)

# what is covered
tf_media()
tf_factions()
tf_teams()
table(tf_characters$team, tf_characters$medium)

# palette names, optionally for one faction, team or role
tf_palette_names()
tf_palette_names(team = "Constructicons")
tf_palette_names(role = "combined form")

# the colours of one character (prints the swatches and the hex codes)
tf_palette("optimus_prime")
#> Transformers palette 'optimus_prime' (5 colours, toy)
#> Autobot: Optimus Prime
#> #D0202A #1F3E8F #B8BABF #F2D23C #2D2D2D

# first three colours, a 12-step gradient, or the same gradient dark-to-light
tf_palette("Megatron", 3)
tf_palette("devastator", 12, type = "continuous")
tf_palette("hot_spot", 12, type = "continuous", sort = TRUE)

# swatches with hex codes, for a team or faction at a time
tf_show_palettes(team = "Aerialbots")
tf_show_palettes(faction = "Decepticon", role = "combined form", ncol = 3)
```

![Leaders and combined
forms](reference/figures/palettes-leaders-and-combiners.png)

Leaders and combined forms

### Toy, cartoon or comic

Every function takes a `medium` argument that defaults to `"toy"`, so
the plain names always give the toy colours. Ask for `"cartoon"` to get
the flat colours of the Sunbow animation model, or `"comic"` for the
Marvel colouring where one exists. The full names with a suffix work
too.

``` r

tf_palette("drag_strip")                      # yellow-orange and plum toy
tf_palette("drag_strip", medium = "cartoon")  # yellow and purple cartoon model
tf_palette("megatron_comic")                  # same as medium = "comic"

tf_palette_names(medium = "cartoon")
tf_palette_names(role = "leader", medium = "all")
tf_show_palettes(c("optimus_prime", "optimus_prime_cartoon", "optimus_prime_comic"), ncol = 1)
tf_team_palette("Constructicons", medium = "cartoon")   # lime green, not grass green
```

![Toy, cartoon and comic
versions](reference/figures/media-comparison.png)

Toy, cartoon and comic versions

Every character has a cartoon palette; the Seacons’ comes from the
Japanese Super-God Masterforce series, since they never appeared in the
Sunbow show. Comic palettes exist for Optimus Prime and Megatron so far,
and the teams are queued in
[`WISHLIST.md`](https://bmaitner.github.io/transformerpalettes/WISHLIST.md):
Marvel colouring changed from issue to issue, so each one is added from
a named issue rather than from memory. Asking for a medium a character
does not have yet gives an error that says so.

### Team palettes

[`tf_team_palette()`](https://bmaitner.github.io/transformerpalettes/reference/tf_team_palette.md)
takes one colour from each member of a combiner team, in the team’s
order (torso first, then limbs), and names each colour after the member
it came from. The body colours are faithful but collapse for teams cast
from shared plastics, so `distinct = TRUE` picks, for each member, the
colour from its palette that is furthest from the colours chosen so far.

``` r

tf_team_palette("Stunticons")
#> Transformers team palette 'stunticons' (5 colours)
#> motormaster = #1E1E1E
#> dead_end = #7A1F2E
#> breakdown = #F0F0EC
#> drag_strip = #F2C21E
#> wildrider = #4E5257

tf_team_palette("Constructicons")                  # six shades of green
tf_team_palette("Constructicons", distinct = TRUE) # green, purple, silver, ...
```

![Team palettes](reference/figures/team-palettes.png)

Team palettes

### ggplot2

[`scale_colour_tf()`](https://bmaitner.github.io/transformerpalettes/reference/scale_tf.md)
and
[`scale_fill_tf()`](https://bmaitner.github.io/transformerpalettes/reference/scale_tf.md)
build a discrete scale by default, or a continuous gradient with
`discrete = FALSE`. The explicit `_d` and `_c` variants and the American
`scale_color_*` spellings are also exported. `sort = TRUE` on a
continuous scale orders the palette from darkest to lightest first. Team
palettes go through
[`scale_colour_manual()`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/scale_manual.html).

``` r

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, colour = drv)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_colour_tf("optimus_prime")

ggplot(diamonds, aes(cut, fill = cut)) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_fill_tf("predaking")

ggplot(faithfuld, aes(waiting, eruptions, fill = density)) +
  geom_raster() +
  scale_fill_tf_c("hot_spot", sort = TRUE)

ggplot(economics_long, aes(date, value01, colour = variable)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = unname(tf_team_palette("Combaticons")))

ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, colour = drv)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_colour_tf("optimus_prime", medium = "cartoon")
```

![Example ggplot2 scales](reference/figures/examples.png)

Example ggplot2 scales

Set `reverse = TRUE` to flip a palette. If a discrete variable has more
levels than a palette has colours, the palette is interpolated so every
level still gets a colour, at some cost to legibility.

### Finding a palette that works for a plot

Toy colours were chosen to look good on a shelf, not on a chart.
[`tf_find_palettes()`](https://bmaitner.github.io/transformerpalettes/reference/tf_find_palettes.md)
shortlists the palettes whose colours hold up for a given job, judged
from the colours themselves:

``` r

tf_find_palettes("categorical")   # every pair of colours clearly distinct
tf_find_palettes("colorblind")    # still distinct under simulated CVD
tf_find_palettes("sequential")    # one hue, wide lightness range
tf_find_palettes("diverging")     # two hues with a light colour between

# restrict to a faction or team, or see the shortlist as swatches
tf_find_palettes("colorblind", faction = "Autobot")
tf_show_palettes(use = "colorblind", ncol = 3)
```

![Colorblind-friendly
shortlist](reference/figures/palettes-colorblind.png)

Colorblind-friendly shortlist

The judgments come from
[`tf_palette_stats()`](https://bmaitner.github.io/transformerpalettes/reference/tf_palette_stats.md),
which reports the smallest pairwise distance between colours in CIE Lab,
the same after simulating deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia, the
lightness range, and the hue spread. The thresholds are simple
heuristics, so treat the result as a shortlist to look at rather than a
guarantee.

### Picking the best few colours from one or more palettes

Whole palettes are faithful to the characters, not to the chart.
[`tf_pick()`](https://bmaitner.github.io/transformerpalettes/reference/tf_pick.md)
pools the colours of the palettes you name, drops any that would not
read against the background (white for `"light"` and `"greyscale"`,
near-black for `"dark"`, judged by WCAG contrast), and then chooses the
`n` colours whose closest pair is farthest apart in CIE Lab. With
`colorblind = TRUE` the distance is the worst case across simulated
deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia; with `style = "greyscale"` only
lightness counts, so the result survives a black-and-white printer.

``` r

# five colours for a white-background plot, from the two leaders
tf_pick(c("optimus_prime", "megatron"), n = 5)
#> Transformers pick of 5 colours from optimus_prime + megatron
#> light background #FFFFFF, min distance 21.7
#> optimus_prime = #D0202A
#> optimus_prime = #1F3E8F
#> megatron = #8C9095
#> megatron = #2A2A2A
#> megatron = #6B3FA0

# four colour-blind-safe colours for a dark theme, from a whole team
tf_pick(tf_palette_names(team = "Combaticons"), n = 4,
        style = "dark", colorblind = TRUE)

# printable in greyscale, using the cartoon colours
tf_pick(tf_palette_names(team = "Stunticons"), n = 4,
        style = "greyscale", medium = "cartoon")

ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, colour = drv)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = unname(tf_pick(c("optimus_prime", "megatron"), 3)))
```

![tf_pick examples](reference/figures/pick-examples.png)

tf_pick examples

Each colour is named after the palette it came from, and the
`min_distance` attribute reports how separable the closest pair is
(above 20 is comfortable, below about 12 is risky). The contrast filter
is strict on purpose: saturated yellows fail it against white, so a
light-mode pick from the Predacons has fewer colours to work with. Lower
`min_contrast` to keep them, or pass a different `background`.

### Character background

`tf_characters` is a data frame with one row per palette: the character,
which medium the palette records, faction, combiner team and combined
form, its role in the team, alternate mode, the year of the toy or first
appearance, a description of the colours, and links to the character’s
page and the reference image (toy photo, episode still or comic panel)
on the Transformers Wiki.

``` r

t(tf_characters[tf_characters$palette == "drag_strip", ])
#> palette     "drag_strip"
#> base        "drag_strip"
#> medium      "toy"
#> character   "Drag Strip"
#> faction     "Decepticon"
#> team        "Stunticons"
#> combiner    "menasor"
#> role        "combiner limb"
#> alt_mode    "Tyrrell P34 six-wheeled race car"
#> year        "1986"
#> n_colours   "5"
#> description "Yellow-orange race car plastic with dark plum head and blaster, ..."
#> source      "https://tfwiki.net/wiki/Drag_Strip_(G1)"
#> image       "https://tfwiki.net/mediawiki/images2/c/c2/G1Dragstrip_toy.jpg"
```

## Coverage

| Team | Faction | Members | Combined form | Year | Media |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|
| (leaders) | both | Optimus Prime, Megatron |  | 1984 | toy, cartoon, comic |
| Aerialbots | Autobot | Silverbolt, Air Raid, Fireflight, Skydive, Slingshot | Superion | 1986 | toy, cartoon |
| Protectobots | Autobot | Hot Spot, Streetwise, Blades, Groove, First Aid | Defensor | 1986 | toy, cartoon |
| Technobots | Autobot | Scattershot, Lightspeed, Nosecone, Strafe, Afterburner | Computron | 1987 | toy, cartoon |
| Constructicons | Decepticon | Hook, Long Haul, Scrapper, Bonecrusher, Mixmaster, Scavenger | Devastator | 1985 | toy, cartoon |
| Stunticons | Decepticon | Motormaster, Dead End, Breakdown, Drag Strip, Wildrider | Menasor | 1986 | toy, cartoon |
| Combaticons | Decepticon | Onslaught, Brawl, Swindle, Blast Off, Vortex | Bruticus | 1986 | toy, cartoon |
| Terrorcons | Decepticon | Hun-Gurrr, Blot, Cutthroat, Rippersnapper, Sinnertwin | Abominus | 1987 | toy, cartoon |
| Predacons | Decepticon | Razorclaw, Rampage, Tantrum, Headstrong, Divebomb | Predaking | 1986 | toy, cartoon |
| Seacons | Decepticon | Snaptrap, Nautilator, Overbite, Seawing, Skalor, Tentakil | Piranacon | 1988 | toy, cartoon (Masterforce) |

Palette names are the character’s name in snake_case (`hun_gurrr`,
`blast_off`);
[`tf_palette()`](https://bmaitner.github.io/transformerpalettes/reference/tf_palette.md)
also accepts `"Hun-Gurrr"` and `"Blast Off"`. Every team is drawn in
`man/figures/palettes-<team>.png`. Characters and teams that are lined
up to be added next are listed in
[`WISHLIST.md`](https://bmaitner.github.io/transformerpalettes/WISHLIST.md);
add a line there, or open a
[request](https://github.com/bmaitner/transformerpalettes/issues/new?template=new-character.yml).

## How the palettes were made

There is no published set of hex values for Transformers toys, so these
are approximations built by hand:

1.  Each character was matched to its original Hasbro release on the
    [Transformers Wiki](https://tfwiki.net/), and to the wiki’s photo of
    that toy in robot mode. The page and the photo are the `source` and
    `image` columns of `tf_characters`.
2.  The plastic, chrome, die-cast and paint colours of that toy were
    listed from the photo and the wiki’s own description of the release,
    and a hex value chosen for each by eye. Colours are ordered body
    plastic first, then secondary plastic, then accents, so the first
    few colours in each palette are the most distinct.
3.  Members of one combiner team share plastics, so their palettes share
    hex values on purpose. The combined form’s palette takes one colour
    from each contributing part.

Cartoon palettes were read the same way from an episode still on the
wiki, which the browser links to; they use the flat colours of the
animation model, so a cartoon palette is typically brighter and simpler
than its toy. Comic palettes name the Marvel issue they were taken from.

Palettes range from four to six colours. Chrome and die-cast parts do
not reduce to a single flat colour; a silver or grey stands in for them.
Wiki photos vary in lighting, so expect some palettes to be rough, and
the least certain ones are flagged in
[`WISHLIST.md`](https://bmaitner.github.io/transformerpalettes/WISHLIST.md).
Corrections are welcome, ideally with a photograph of the toy under
neutral light. Use the [palette
browser](https://bmaitner.github.io/transformerpalettes/articles/browse.html)
to open a prefilled issue for a specific palette, or pick a form from
the [issue
templates](https://github.com/bmaitner/transformerpalettes/issues/new/choose).
[`tf_show_palettes()`](https://bmaitner.github.io/transformerpalettes/reference/tf_show_palettes.md)
prints the hex codes under each swatch to make reporting easy.

## Trademarks

Transformers, Autobot, Decepticon and the character names used here are
trademarks of Hasbro and Takara Tomy. This package only records
approximate colour values and uses the names to refer to them.

# Package index

## Palettes

- [`tf_palettes`](https://bmaitner.github.io/transformerpalettes/reference/tf_palettes.md)
  : Generation 1 Transformers palettes
- [`tf_characters`](https://bmaitner.github.io/transformerpalettes/reference/tf_characters.md)
  : Generation 1 Transformers character metadata
- [`tf_palette()`](https://bmaitner.github.io/transformerpalettes/reference/tf_palette.md)
  : Get colours from a character's palette
- [`tf_team_palette()`](https://bmaitner.github.io/transformerpalettes/reference/tf_team_palette.md)
  : One colour per member of a combiner team
- [`tf_palette_names()`](https://bmaitner.github.io/transformerpalettes/reference/tf_palette_names.md)
  : List the available palettes
- [`tf_media()`](https://bmaitner.github.io/transformerpalettes/reference/tf_media.md)
  [`tf_factions()`](https://bmaitner.github.io/transformerpalettes/reference/tf_media.md)
  [`tf_teams()`](https://bmaitner.github.io/transformerpalettes/reference/tf_media.md)
  : List the media, factions and combiner teams in transformerpalettes
- [`tf_show_palettes()`](https://bmaitner.github.io/transformerpalettes/reference/tf_show_palettes.md)
  : Display Transformers palettes

## Choosing colours for a plot

- [`tf_pick()`](https://bmaitner.github.io/transformerpalettes/reference/tf_pick.md)
  : Pick the most distinguishable colours from one or more palettes
- [`tf_find_palettes()`](https://bmaitner.github.io/transformerpalettes/reference/tf_find_palettes.md)
  : Find Transformers palettes that suit a plotting use case
- [`tf_palette_stats()`](https://bmaitner.github.io/transformerpalettes/reference/tf_palette_stats.md)
  : Perceptual statistics for every Transformers palette
